extracted.intended_audience: students enrolled in (or considering) MIT OpenCourseWare 'Calculus with Theory' (single-variable calculus with emphasis on proofs)
extracted.subtask_description: Syllabus and course policies for an undergraduate single-variable calculus course taught with an emphasis on proofs and conceptual understanding (MIT OCW). Includes schedule, topics, textbooks, assignment/exam structure, and grading rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course emphasis / description
rubrics_metrics.description: We will cover the same material as 18.01 but with an emphasis on proofs and conceptual understanding rather than computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include axioms for the real numbers; the Riemann integral; limits, theorems on continuous functions; derivatives of functions of one variable; the fundamental theorems of calculus; Taylor’s theorem; infinite series, power series, rigorous treatment of the elementary functions. (This establishes the course's pedagogical goal: proof-based, conceptual mastery rather than computational skill.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: We will assume a working knowledge of Calculus I (18.01 Single Variable Calculus), but no familiarity with proofs or proof writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should know basic single-variable calculus material entering the course; previous exposure to formal proof techniques is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required textbook / materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Apostol, Tom M. Calculus, Volume 1: One-Variable Calculus, with An Introduction to Linear Algebra. (Vol. 2 will be needed for those who wish to continue on to 18.024 Multivariable calculus with theory.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional course notes by James Raymond Munkres are provided. Apostol Vol. 1 is the primary text for the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lecture and recitation meeting times
rubrics_metrics.description: Lectures: 3 sessions / week, 1 hour / session; Recitations: 2 sessions / week, 1 hour / session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the expected in-person/meeting time commitment and structure of the course (lecture vs recitation components).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recitation preparation and presentation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of each unit, students will receive a schedule that includes problems to complete in advance of the next recitation. Students should be prepared to present their proofs in clear detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recitations are active: students must do assigned problems before class and be ready to present proofs clearly. This is intended to give students the opportunity to deliberately improve their proof writing skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem set frequency and due policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem sets are assigned weekly, and due the following week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem sets form a regular, weekly assessed component; punctual completion is implied by weekly due dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem set score replacement policy
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the course, the lowest two pset scores for each student will be replaced by his or her average score on all of the psets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring guidance: two lowest weekly problem-set grades are effectively 'smoothed' by substituting the student's overall pset average, reducing the impact of outlier low scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exams: number, format, and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be three in-class, one hour exams, and one three-hour comprehensive final exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calendar indicates coverage: Hour exam I covers lectures 1-9; Hour exam II covers lectures 10-20; Hour exam III covers lectures 21-29; Final exam is comprehensive. This defines assessment timing and topical scope for each midterm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading breakdown (weights)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACTIVITIES PERCENTAGES — Problem sets 20%; Midterms 40%; Final exam 30%; Participation 10%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how course performance is quantified and how much each activity contributes to the final grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course calendar / topic schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Lecture-by-lecture topics with key dates and pset due dates (e.g., Lectures 0–4: Real numbers, proof writing, axioms of reals, integers/induction; Pset1 due after lecture covering integral definition; Hour exams and which lectures they cover).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed sequencing of topics and alignment with problem-set deadlines and exam dates — provides expectations for pacing, which topics will be emphasized when, and when assessments occur.
